content.comment_body: Hello, For communication between several [product_name], due to the distance, fiber is used (connected to a network card). When the fiber network connection is lost, the last data on the network remains unchanged (variables do not update). If the network socket is removed from [product_name], alarms are triggered, but when fiber is disconnected, there is no reaction—the device keeps working with the last available data.

Hello [user_name], I am not sure what you mean by "fiber communication network" and "network socket." Could you clarify? Which network card are you referring to? How are you monitoring or diagnosing the network communication?

Hello, If [product_name] is connected to a physical ethernet port (such as a switch with only [product_name] attached), it will not detect network failures. The fiber-to-ethernet converter behaves similarly, so removing the fiber still makes [product_name] think the connection exists. You could try enabling the Keep Alive option in the connection settings, which might prompt [product_name] to show an error. I cannot confirm this myself since I recently installed my last [article_no]. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: The central concern involves the inability of [product_name] devices to recognize fiber network disconnections when a fiber-to-ethernet converter is used. While unplugging the network socket generates alarms, physically disconnecting the fiber causes the device to rely on outdated data, as if the network were still functioning—affecting the reliability of network status detection.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to detect any loss in network connectivity, including fiber disconnections, and promptly trigger a relevant alarm or reaction.
